request.spec: The householdId must become deterministic: the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 over (normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode), so owners with the same lastName and postcode share it automatically. This changes existing behaviour: 'sharesHousehold' now only bypasses the duplicate block rather than creating the link, and everything that keys off the household (duplicate detection and the household-size input to the membership level) must use this computed householdId. Because the household is now keyed on (lastName, postcode), owners sharing lastName and postcode are the same household: a second such owner is rejected as a household duplicate (409) unless it sets 'sharesHousehold', in which case it is created as a declared household member and is NOT flagged as a possible duplicate (a declared member is not a suspected duplicate).
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

The householdId must become deterministic: the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 over (normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode), so owners with the same lastName and postcode share it automatically. This changes existing behaviour: 'sharesHousehold' now only bypasses the duplicate block rather than creating the link, and everything that keys off the household (duplicate detection and the household-size input to the membership level) must use this computed householdId. Because the household is now keyed on (lastName, postcode), owners sharing lastName and postcode are the same household: a second such owner is rejected as a household duplicate (409) unless it sets 'sharesHousehold', in which case it is created as a declared household member and is NOT flagged as a possible duplicate (a declared member is not a suspected duplicate).

agent.result_text:
Tests green. Both findings addressed — I agreed with both:

**Finding 1 — duplicated derivation / no `ofOwner`-style overload.** Added `HouseholdKey.householdId(Owner owner)` mirroring `IdentityKey.ofOwner`, so "which two fields make a household" lives in one place. Switched all owner-entity call sites to it:
- `AssignHousehold` → `householdId(owner)`
- `RequireUniqueIdentity` → the existing-owner recompute now uses `householdId(existing)` (the candidate stays `householdId(lastName, postcode)` since it comes from the `OwnerFieldsDto` request, not an `Owner`)
- `AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate` → both the new owner and each existing owner go through `householdId(owner)` / `householdId(existing)`

On the related sub-point (line 35's `IdentityKey.ofOwner(existing)` reads the *stored* `householdId` while the household check recomputes): I kept the household check recomputing, now behind the single overload. Recomputing is deliberate — it keys purely on `(lastName, postcode)` as the spec demands, so it also catches any owner (e.g. seed rows) whose stored id is null or predates the deterministic scheme, rather than trusting a possibly-absent stored value. Consolidating behind the one accessor removes the "two spellings of the same derivation" that the reviewer flagged.

**Finding 2 — stale address cross-references.** Updated `AddressNormalizer`'s and `NormalizeOwnerAddress`'s javadoc: `HouseholdKey` no longer compares the normalized address, so I removed those claims and noted the household id is keyed on `(lastName, postcode)`. `AddressNormalizer` still references `HouseholdKey` only to point out it does *not* use the address, keeping the documented invariant true.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The behavioural rework is well-factored — `HouseholdKey` collapsing from an instantiated key into a single static `householdId(lastName, postcode)`, reusing `Hashes.sha256Hex`, and moving the `sharesHousehold` semantics into the two consumers all read cleanly. Two structural issues remain, both about the codebase's own "single definition, cannot drift apart" idiom.

**1. Duplicated "owner → householdId" derivation; no `ofOwner`-style overload.**
`HouseholdKey.householdId(x.getLastName(), x.getPostcode())` now appears five times across three classes:
- `AssignHousehold:19`
- `RequireUniqueIdentity:31` and `:39`
- `AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate:37` and `:42`

This codebase already establishes the pattern for this exact situation: `IdentityKey` offers both `of(raw parts)` and `ofOwner(Owner)` so callers never repeat the field-plucking. `HouseholdKey` should mirror it with an overload, e.g. `static String householdId(Owner owner)` (or `ofOwner`), so the `(getLastName(), getPostcode())` tuple lives in one place. As written, the knowledge of "which two fields make a household" is re-scattered across the callers — the very drift the class javadoc claims to prevent.

Relatedly, inside `RequireUniqueIdentity`'s loop an existing owner's household id is obtained two different ways in the same iteration: recomputed via `HouseholdKey.householdId(existing.getLastName(), existing.getPostcode())` at line 39, while line 35's `IdentityKey.ofOwner(existing)` reads the stored `existing.getHouseholdId()`. Two paths to the same value for the same object is the kind of inconsistency a maintainer will trip over; consolidating behind one accessor removes it.

**2. Stale cross-references left in the address-normalization files.**
`HouseholdKey` no longer touches the address, but the files describing that former relationship weren't updated and now assert something false:
- `AddressNormalizer.java:7-9` — "Shared by ... `{@link HouseholdKey}` (which compares against it for duplicate detection and the shared household id)". HouseholdKey no longer uses the normalized address at all.
- `NormalizeOwnerAddress.java:9-11` — "`{@link AssignHousehold}` and `{@link HouseholdKey}` compare the normalized form". Neither does anymore.

The rest of the diff is scrupulous about keeping javadoc in sync (the updates to `HouseholdKey`, `RequireUniqueIdentity`, `AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate`, and `openapi.yml` are all accurate), which makes these two dangling references stand out. Update them to reflect that the household id is now keyed on `(lastName, postcode)` so the documented invariant actually holds.
